title: Iraola Provides Worrying Three-Word Update on Szoboszlai Injury
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:00 AM EDTDominik Szoboszlai barely lasted half an hour against Brentford. / Glyn KIRK/AFP/Getty ImagesLONDON — Dominik Szoboszlai’s return to Liverpool’s starting XI lasted for just 32 minutes before he was forced off after aggravating an existing injury against Brentford, prompting Andoni Iraola to predict that he will be out “for some time.”
The all-action Hungarian midfielder had missed Liverpool’s previous two fixtures with a hamstring issue, failing to even travel to Austria for the midweek Champions League win over LASK.

Andoni Iraola had been uncertain of Szoboszlai’s fitness heading into Saturday’s trip to Brentford but was convinced by Thursday and Friday’s training sessions to start his first-choice midfielder alongside Alexis Mac Allister. That decision spectacularly backfired.

Szoboszlai crumpled in a heap on the turf half an hour into the Premier League clash in west London, entirely unconnected to any other player. Liverpool’s medical staff made the short trip from the dugout to the nearside of the halfway line but the player’s mind had been made up. With a disconsolate shake of his head, Szoboszlai trudged off the pitch and down the tunnel.

Liverpool were already understaffed in the middle of the pitch by Ryan Gravenberch’s suspension and promptly conceded a cheap header to trail during the interval. They would recover to win 2–1 but Iraola ominously described the victory as “very expensive.”

Dominik Szoboszlai cut a disappointed figure. / Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesThere had been no contact on Szoboszlai—the midfielder had in fact been sticking to a more disciplined deeper role during a promising half-hour of action—and the worst fears of a recurrence of his recent muscular issue were realized.
Iraola admitted that the quick turnaround in fixtures had afforded his players “not the proper recovery” and Szoboszlai’s ailment had “not healed enough.”

The 25-year-old had been mercifully spared any serious injuries over the last few years. The hamstring problem which forced him to miss the thumping from Manchester City and win over LASK was his first fitness complaint since February 2024.
Back then, Szoboszlai missed 10 Liverpool matches in quick succession with a hamstring issue which has not flared up again—until now.

Andoni Iraola cannot catch a break. / Glyn KIRK/AFP/Getty ImagesOnly the fullness of time will reveal a detailed timeline but Iraola admitted that he will be without the Hungary international “for some time.” That Szoboszlai has just come back from such a recent setback will be a concern.
Iraola already has personnel issues in the middle of the pitch given Gravenberch’s current suspension—although the Netherlands international will be available from Monday onward.

“We need everyone,” Iraola breathlessly warned, “we will need everyone in one moment or the other. Everyone has to be ready because we will need him probably.” Szoboszlai won’t be ready in the immediate future.
